papers.title: A Physics-Enforced Neural Network to Predict Polymer Melt Viscosity
papers.abstract: Achieving superior polymeric components through additive manufacturing (AM) relies on precise control of rheology. One key rheological property particularly relevant to AM is melt viscosity ($η$). Melt viscosity is influenced by polymer chemistry, molecular weight ($M_w$), polydispersity, induced shear rate ($\dotγ$), and processing temperature ($T$). The relationship of $η$ with $M_w$, $\dotγ$, and $T$ may be captured by parameterized equations. Several physical experiments are required to fit the parameters, so predicting $η$ of a new polymer material in unexplored physical domains is a laborious process. Here, we develop a Physics-Enforced Neural Network (PENN) model that predicts the empirical parameters and encodes the parametrized equations to calculate $η$ as a function of polymer chemistry, $M_w$, polydispersity, $\dotγ$, and $T$. We benchmark our PENN against physics-unaware Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) models. Finally, we demonstrate that the PENN offers superior values of $η$ when extrapolating to unseen values of $M_w$, $\dotγ$, and $T$ for sparsely seen polymers.

summary_zh.method: 提出物理强制神经网络(PENN)编码参数化方程预测粘度。

summary_en.motivation: Predicting polymer melt viscosity for additive manufacturing requires numerous physical experiments, motivating a data-efficient model.
summary_en.method: A Physics-Enforced Neural Network (PENN) encodes parameterized equations to predict viscosity as a function of chemistry, molecular weight, shear rate, and temperature.
summary_en.result: PENN outperforms physics-unaware ANN and GPR in extrapolating to unseen conditions for sparsely seen polymers.
summary_en.validation: Benchmarked against ANN and GPR on numerical datasets without experimental validation.

papers.title: SEF: A Method for Computing Prediction Intervals by Shifting the Error Function in Neural Networks
papers.abstract: In today's era, Neural Networks (NN) are applied in various scientific fields such as robotics, medicine, engineering, etc. However, the predictions of neural networks themselves contain a degree of uncertainty that must always be taken into account before any decision is made. This is why many researchers have focused on developing different ways to quantify the uncertainty of neural network predictions. Some of these methods are based on generating prediction intervals (PI) via neural networks for the requested target values. The SEF (Shifting the Error Function) method presented in this paper is a new method that belongs to this category of methods. The proposed approach involves training a single neural network three times, thus generating an estimate along with the corresponding upper and lower bounds for a given problem. A pivotal aspect of the method is the calculation of a parameter from the initial network's estimates, which is then integrated into the loss functions of the other two networks. This innovative process effectively produces PIs, resulting in a robust and efficient technique for uncertainty quantification. To evaluate the effectiveness of our method, a comparison in terms of successful PI generation between the SEF, PI3NN and PIVEN methods was made using two synthetic datasets.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法提出了一种新的神经网络预测区间生成技术，可迁移用于生物力学代理模型的不确定性量化。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not apply the method to FEA surrogate modeling or biomechanical design, and lacks validation on engineering or biomedical problems.

summary_zh.motivation: 神经网络预测存在不确定性，需要量化方法。
summary_zh.method: 通过三次训练单个神经网络并调整误差函数生成预测区间。
summary_zh.result: 在合成数据集上，SEF方法生成的预测区间优于PI3NN和PIVEN。
summary_zh.validation: 在两个合成数据集上与其他方法对比验证。

summary_en.motivation: Neural network predictions inherently involve uncertainty that must be quantified for reliable decision-making.
summary_en.method: The SEF method trains a single neural network three times, using a parameter derived from the initial network's estimates to shift the error function in the loss of the other two networks, thereby producing prediction intervals.
summary_en.result: On two synthetic datasets, SEF generates more effective prediction intervals compared to PI3NN and PIVEN methods.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on synthetic datasets by comparing the quality of prediction intervals against existing methods.

papers.title: Inference for Large Scale Regression Models with Dependent Errors
papers.abstract: The exponential growth in data sizes and storage costs has brought considerable challenges to the data science community, requiring solutions to run learning methods on such data. While machine learning has scaled to achieve predictive accuracy in big data settings, statistical inference and uncertainty quantification tools are still lagging. Priority scientific fields collect vast data to understand phenomena typically studied with statistical methods like regression. In this setting, regression parameter estimation can benefit from efficient computational procedures, but the main challenge lies in computing error process parameters with complex covariance structures. Identifying and estimating these structures is essential for inference and often used for uncertainty quantification in machine learning with Gaussian Processes. However, estimating these structures becomes burdensome as data scales, requiring approximations that compromise the reliability of outputs. These approximations are even more unreliable when complexities like long-range dependencies or missing data are present. This work defines and proves the statistical properties of the Generalized Method of Wavelet Moments with Exogenous variables (GMWMX), a highly scalable, stable, and statistically valid method for estimating and delivering inference for linear models using stochastic processes in the presence of data complexities like latent dependence structures and missing data. Applied examples from Earth Sciences and extensive simulations highlight the advantages of the GMWMX.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address surrogate modeling for FEA, constraint handling, or uncertainty quantification in biomechanical implant design; it focuses on statistical inference for regression with dependent errors in Earth Sciences.

summary_zh.motivation: 大规模数据中回归模型误差依赖结构的推断困难。
summary_zh.method: 提出广义小波矩方法(GMWMX)处理复杂协方差结构。
summary_zh.result: GMWMX在模拟和地球科学应用中表现出可扩展性和统计有效性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过模拟和地球科学实例验证。

summary_en.motivation: Statistical inference for large-scale regression models with complex error dependencies remains computationally challenging.
summary_en.method: The Generalized Method of Wavelet Moments with Exogenous variables (GMWMX) is proposed to estimate and perform inference for linear models with dependent errors.
summary_en.result: GMWMX provides scalable, stable, and statistically valid inference, demonstrated on Earth Science data and simulations.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed through extensive simulations and applied examples from Earth Sciences.

papers.title: Sampling recovery in Bochner spaces and applications to parametric PDEs
papers.abstract: We prove convergence rates of linear sampling recovery of functions in abstract Bochner spaces satisfying weighted summability of their generalized polynomial chaos expansion coefficients. The underlying algorithm is a function-valued extension of the least squares method widely used and thoroughly studied in scalar-valued function recovery. We apply our theory to two core problems in Computational Uncertainty Quantification. First, we address non-intrusive approximations of solutions to parametric elliptic or parabolic PDEs with log-normal or affine inputs using a finite set of particular solvers. Second, we consider approximating infinite-dimensional holomorphic functions that arise as solutions to more general parametric PDEs with Gaussian random field inputs. Our framework allows a unified treatment of the log-normal and affine input models and yields substantial improvements in the state of the art of these problems. More specifically, we obtain convergence rates that improve known results by a polynomial factor in the log-normal case and by a logarithmic factor in the affine case.

summary_zh.method: 将标量最小二乘法扩展到函数值Bochner空间
summary_zh.result: 在对数正态和仿射输入模型下改进了收敛率

summary_en.motivation: To improve the convergence rates of linear sampling recovery for solutions of parametric PDEs in Bochner spaces.
summary_en.method: Extends the scalar-valued least squares method to function-valued recovery in Bochner spaces with weighted polynomial chaos expansions.
summary_en.result: Achieves improved convergence rates by a polynomial factor for log-normal inputs and a logarithmic factor for affine inputs.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical proofs only, without numerical benchmarks or simulation cases.

papers.title: Deep Bayesian Active Learning-to-Rank with Relative Annotation for Estimation of Ulcerative Colitis Severity
papers.abstract: Automatic image-based severity estimation is an important task in computer-aided diagnosis. Severity estimation by deep learning requires a large amount of training data to achieve a high performance. In general, severity estimation uses training data annotated with discrete (i.e., quantized) severity labels. Annotating discrete labels is often difficult in images with ambiguous severity, and the annotation cost is high. In contrast, relative annotation, in which the severity between a pair of images is compared, can avoid quantizing severity and thus makes it easier. We can estimate relative disease severity using a learning-to-rank framework with relative annotations, but relative annotation has the problem of the enormous number of pairs that can be annotated. Therefore, the selection of appropriate pairs is essential for relative annotation. In this paper, we propose a deep Bayesian active learning-to-rank that automatically selects appropriate pairs for relative annotation. Our method preferentially annotates unlabeled pairs with high learning efficiency from the model uncertainty of the samples. We prove the theoretical basis for adapting Bayesian neural networks to pairwise learning-to-rank and demonstrate the efficiency of our method through experiments on endoscopic images of ulcerative colitis on both private and public datasets. We also show that our method achieves a high performance under conditions of significant class imbalance because it automatically selects samples from the minority classes.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关注医学图像中的疾病严重程度估计，与用户的研究方向（FEA代理建模、植入物设计）无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses medical image severity estimation, not surrogate modeling for FEA or implant design; no contact mechanics, no structural optimization, no uncertainty quantification for physical simulations.

summary_zh.motivation: 减少相对标注中大量配对的人工成本
summary_zh.method: 提出深度贝叶斯主动学习排序，自动选择高信息量的图像对进行标注
summary_zh.result: 在溃疡性结肠炎内镜图像上实现了高效且准确的严重程度估计
summary_zh.validation: 在私有和公开数据集上验证，并处理了类别不平衡问题

summary_en.motivation: To reduce the annotation cost of relative severity labeling by automatically selecting informative image pairs.
summary_en.method: A deep Bayesian active learning-to-rank framework that selects pairs with high model uncertainty for annotation.
summary_en.result: Achieved efficient and accurate severity estimation on endoscopic images of ulcerative colitis, even under class imbalance.
summary_en.validation: Validated on private and public datasets with clinical endoscopic images.
